- When sentiment is consistently neutral or negative (0.00), model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for 30-day horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior period), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in subsequent periods.
- If sentiment shows early positive signals (e.g., 0.20–0.67), model underreacts; increase forecast by 2–5% to align with sentiment momentum.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias in flat sentiment periods — if 18-day history is stable, forecast should not drift >1.5% from recent 5-day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows early sharp decline (e.g., 3–5 days of drop), model often fails to anticipate; add 1–2% downward bias starting from day 5.
- When sentiment is positive but recent prices are falling, model may overcorrect; reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid “over-optimism” in bullish sentiment.
